about: Fixed drafting prompts for the S-3.3.4 voice-match harness, written before any draft was generated (pre-registered in docs/notes/2026-10-19-voice-match-preregistration.md). Each is a situation the synthetic writer (personas.json) would write a short note about, in their own domain. Both conditions are told the writer's language, so a voice win is about style, not language.

asha: A news article says a new import duty on electronics will protect domestic jobs.
A friend forwards a study claiming remote work raises productivity by 13 percent.
A video argues the central bank should cut rates because inflation feels lower.
A founder on a podcast credits their success to waking up at 5 a.m. every day.
A report says exports in a new sector grew 40 percent last quarter.
An influencer says a single chart proves the housing market will crash.
bharat: A popular documentary blames the Mughal decline on one emperor's policies.
A lecture claims the railways in colonial India were built mainly for Indians' benefit.
A review praises a new history of the 1857 uprising for its simple, clear story.
A podcast compares the British Empire to Rome.
An article describes the 1950s as a golden age of Indian planning.
A talk argues the Permanent Settlement of 1793 was a complete failure.
chetan: A quick-commerce startup raised a huge round and promises 10-minute delivery everywhere.
A founder posts that their app hit one million downloads in its first month.
An investor says profitability does not matter in a startup's first five years.
A friend wants to start a D2C brand and spend most of the money on influencer marketing.
A podcast guest says AI will replace all customer-support jobs next year.
A food-delivery company announces it is finally profitable.

languages.chetan: Hinglish (Hindi and English mixed, written in Roman letters)
